title: Where Winds Meet
provenance: Reported by Manas-Taneja (highball-db#277, 2026-10-02, first filed as highball-db#276), Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.9.39, engine x64-crossover26.3-r12 (the Wine 11 engine), DXMT, frame cap 60, rated 4 of 5 after 188 minutes over several sessions, recipes steam, vcrun2022. A second report by the same reporter (highball-db#293, 2026-10-03), same Mac, Highball 0.9.39 and engine x64-crossover26.3-r12, D3DMetal as the environment's mode, frame cap 60, recipes steam and vcrun2022, rated 4 of 5 after 102 minutes with a bit of stutter as the one complaint, the D3DMetal session they mention on highball#240. rishijain754 (highball-db#497, 2026-10-15), Apple M5, macOS 27.0.1, Highball 0.10.15, engine r26, D3DMetal, Windows 11, Metal HUD, AVX advertised, recipes steam, vcrun2022, dotnet48, assetto-corsa and xact, rated 4 of 5 after 5 minutes. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever (highball-db#1297, 2026-11-17, with two follow ups on 2026-11-18), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.28, the Wine 11 engine x64-crossover26.3-r32 and then r33, D3DMetal, rated 3 of 5 (1 of 5 crossed out): not the Steam copy. The Steam install asked for about 200 GB and failed after reserving 165 GB, so the player took the official installer from wherewindsmeetgame.com. It ran in Highball and fetched an 800 MB launcher, which stopped on a Qt dialog, 'Failed to create OpenGL context' for OpenGL 2.0, on the default engine r31 in WineD3D mode (log). CrossOver opened that launcher, and its lite install took 68 GB (105 GB with the pending downloads cancelled). Highball then started Engine/Binaries/Win64r/wwm.exe as an added program. In game on D3DMetal (DXMT and DXVK crashed), it crashed at a boss fight on r32, D3DMetal 4.0 beta 3 by the Metal HUD, the log ending with threads waiting on the process heap lock and exit code 5. On r33, D3DMetal 3, a 50 minute session through a larger boss fight, the Puppeteer, had no crash, at 20 to 25 fps on low settings. With HB_MVK_LENIENT_INTERFACES=1, HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 and HB_X87SIDECAR=1 in the environment, AVX advertised and the Metal HUD on.
notes: Free to play. Reported playable on DXMT on the Wine 11 engine with Highball's frame cap at 60 on an M5 Pro, over sessions of 16 minutes and just over three hours without a crash, and one crash about two and a half minutes into a session with the in-game Store window open. Stutter in areas dense with NPCs. The crash is not a one-off, the reporter counted five in two days on highball#240, from 15 seconds to an hour and a half into a session, always with the same line in the log. It is DXMT's clear pipelines being built before the Metal device field they read was set, fixed in DXMT on 30 September. The default Wine 10 engine has carried the fix since Highball 0.10.1 and the Wine 11 engine gets it in r16, which the 0.10.4 beta ships. A later 102-minute session on D3DMetal on the same r12 had a bit of stutter and no crash in the report, which fits the crash being DXMT's. Whether that session used the game's own DirectX 12 launch option or the default one was not said. Whether the default engine runs it as well is not known, and the anti-cheat map has no entry for this game. No frame rate was given and nothing was measured here. A base M1 played it on D3DMetal on the Wine 11 engine r33 (D3DMetal 3) for 50 minutes without a crash, at 20 to 25 fps on low settings, after a crash at a boss fight on r32 (D3DMetal 4 beta 3). DXMT and DXVK crashed on that Mac. That player installed the game with the official installer's lite option (68 GB) through CrossOver, because the Steam install wanted about 200 GB and the official launcher stops on an OpenGL error in Highball (highball-db#1297).

knownIssues.symptom: Crashes at random, from 15 seconds to an hour and a half into a session, once with the in-game Store window open (reported on an M5 Pro, Wine 11 engine r12, DXMT, highball#240)
knownIssues.cause: DXMT built its clear pipelines before the Metal device field they read was set up, so the request went to whatever that memory held. The 'unrecognized selector sent to instance' line in the log is the signature. Fixed in DXMT on 30 September
knownIssues.fix: The Wine 11 engine carries the fixed DXMT from r16. Environments on it never change revision on their own, so pick the newest, x64-crossover26.3-r19 with Highball 0.10.10, on the environment's Full page under Advanced, Engine. The default engine has it since 0.10.1. D3DMetal avoids it, a 102-minute session there had stutter only

knownIssues.symptom: Stutter in areas with many NPCs on DXMT, and a bit of stutter on D3DMetal too (reported on an M5 Pro)
knownIssues.fix: None known. The reporter plays with Highball's frame cap at 60

knownIssues.symptom: The official launcher from the game's site stops on 'Failed to create OpenGL context' and never opens (M1, the default engine r31, highball-db#1297)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. The launcher is a 32-bit Qt program (Win32/deploy/launcher.exe) asking for OpenGL 2.0. CrossOver opens it
knownIssues.fix: the reporter installed the game through CrossOver, then added Engine/Binaries/Win64r/wwm.exe to Highball as a program

knownIssues.symptom: The Steam install asks for about 200 GB and failed after reserving 165 GB (M1, highball-db#1297)
knownIssues.fix: the official installer's lite install is 68 GB, but its launcher doesn't open in Highball, see above

knownIssues.symptom: Crashed at a boss fight on D3DMetal 4 beta 3 (M1, Wine 11 r32, highball-db#1297)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. The log ends with threads waiting on the process heap lock
knownIssues.fix: the Wine 11 engine r33, with D3DMetal 3, played 50 minutes through a larger boss fight without a crash for the reporter

knownIssues.symptom: DXMT and DXVK crash on a base M1 (highball-db#1297)
